chunks: 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Faddal, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, from Abi Maryam, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام ruled that whatever the judges err in regarding blood money or amputation is upon the public treasury of the Muslims.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: title of Imam 'Ali عليه السلام as the Commander of the Faithful
key_terms.بَيْتِ مَالِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ: the public treasury of the Muslims
key_terms.دِيَةٍ: blood money or financial compensation for unlawful killing or injury
key_terms.قَضَى: issued a legal judgment or ruling
key_terms.قَطْعٍ: amputation or cutting as a judicially imposed bodily penalty

ai.seo_question: Who bears the financial liability when judges make an error in blood money or amputation according to Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a legal ruling from Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام concerning judicial error. It establishes that when judges make a mistake involving blood money or bodily punishment, the financial liability is borne by the Bayt al-Mal of the Muslims rather than left unresolved or imposed arbitrarily.
